stock based pay for new CEOs is sensitive to firm performance and that this sensitivity is higher for new-economy, young, and volatile firms.
the sensitivity of CEO stock based pay to firm performance is higher for firms in new economies, young, volatile firms, and for the CEO's initial year in office.

(1) the sensitivity of CEO stock based pay to firm performance is higher in new economy firms; (2) this is more pronounced in firms that are younger or more volatile; (3) this is more prominent for the CEO's initial year in office.

the role of stock based pay in the process of sorting new CEOs.
the use of stock based compensation for sorting.

the sensitivity of option grants to performance is higher than that of restricted stock grants and is higher for new CEOs than for experienced CEOs.

stock options are a sorting tool for new CEOs and that the sensitivity of option pay to firm performance increases as firms become younger, more new economy and more volatile.

stock based pay is not only used for incentive purposes but also for sorting purposes.
